newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts June jobless rate drops to 3.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts June jobless rate drops to 3.9 pct.

text.p: The Massachusetts seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for June dropped to 3.9 percent, down from the May rate of 4.2 percent, officials said Friday.
The national rate for June unemployment, released on July 3, was 5.0 percent, up from 4.8 percent in May.

"Our average unemployment rate for the last 12 months is 4.0 percent, ranging between 3.8 and 4.2 percent, compared to the U.S. average for the last year of 5.2 percent," Nils Nordberg, deputy director of the state's Division of Employment and Training (DET), said.
Nordberg said the payroll survey of Massachusetts jobs in June showed an estimated gain of 72,600 more jobs than one year ago in June 1996.
